title: Anshul Kamboj Earns Test Recall for New Zealand After Year of Rebuilding
excerpt: Written off after a hard debut at Manchester in 2025, the 25-year-old Haryana pacer forced his way back through domestic cricket, India A and a 21-wicket IPL season.
body:
• Anshul Kamboj, 25, has been recalled to India's 16-man Test squad for the two-match series in New Zealand starting November 19.
  • His only previous Test was a difficult debut at Manchester in 2025: 18 overs, 89 runs, one wicket, after arriving as an injury replacement within 48 hours.
  • He rebuilt through domestic cricket, India A and IPL 2026 with Chennai Super Kings, where he took 21 wickets in 14 matches, and made his ODI debut this month.
  • For diaspora fans, the first Test begins November 19 in Wellington, three days after the final ODI of the tour.

Anshul Kamboj did not hide from his first Test. The Haryana fast bowler made his debut at Manchester in 2025 after Akash Deep and Arshdeep Singh were ruled out, landed in England as an injury replacement and was bowling within 48 hours. England made 669 on a flat pitch; Kamboj bowled 18 overs, conceded 89 runs and took one wicket. More than a year later, he has been recalled to India's Test squad for New Zealand — and, in his own telling to India Today, the work between those two selections is the whole story.

"Give up? No, giving up is never an option. It shouldn't be. You always have to work hard; giving up doesn't stand a chance, it won't do anything."

— Anshul Kamboj, to India Today

Back in the squad

The Board of Control for Cricket in India has named a 16-man squad led by Shubman Gill, with KL Rahul as vice-captain, for two Tests starting November 19 in Wellington and Christchurch, according to Sportskeeda's report of the announcement. Kamboj joins a pace group led by the returning Jasprit Bumrah, with Mohammed Siraj, Prasidh Krishna and the also-recalled Akash Deep. Rishabh Pant's selection is subject to fitness clearance after a side strain in the Irani Cup. India sit fifth in the 2025-27 World Test Championship standings, and this is their last away series of the cycle.

The rebuild, in numbers

Kamboj's route back ran through every level below the Test side. He took 13 wickets in five matches for Haryana in the previous Ranji Trophy season, played India A red-ball matches against Sri Lanka and Australia A, and then produced a productive IPL 2026 for Chennai Super Kings: 21 wickets in 14 matches, including work as a death-overs option with wide yorkers from around the wicket. His childhood coach Satish Rana, who has trained him since he was 10 or 11, says the routine never changed — eight to ten hours a day on the ground since childhood, and a call before every series to plan specific practice.

There were setbacks inside the comeback too. His ODI debut earlier this month, against West Indies in New Chandigarh, cost 82 runs as West Indies chased 352. He answered in Haryana's Ranji Trophy opener against Himachal, taking six wickets. That pattern — a hard day, then immediate domestic work — is what his coach points to. "That Test match in Manchester, I would say our day just went wrong," Rana said. "We just told Anshul to forget about it, focus ahead on his game and work properly."

What New Zealand asks of him

Kamboj has never toured New Zealand and says the trip is first a fact-finding exercise: "It will give me an idea of what lengths I should be mixing and what conditions to expect." He is also in the India A group for three first-class matches, though his ODI squad duties will limit that involvement, before he joins a Test attack where Bumrah sets the standard. At 25, with debuts in two formats behind him, his stated goals are plain: play as much as possible for India and win matches.

What's next

The ODI leg runs first, with the first Test in Wellington on November 19, three days after the final ODI. Whether Kamboj makes the playing XI will depend on conditions and the balance India choose — but after Manchester, simply being selected again is evidence the selectors saw the rebuild, not just the debut.
